speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)

Based on your history of taking haloperidol for tics, combined with your current fever and altered mental status, I am concerned about Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. Since you specifically denied headache, seizures, and sore throat, does the medication list include any other substances, and are you experiencing muscle stiffness or confusion? REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, Creatine Kinase (CK), and Toxicology screen.
